BiblicalUsage: Hobab is the son of Reuel and the father-in-law of Moses, and he is asked to travel with Israel because he knows the wilderness. Moses pleads with him to come and be their eyes in the desert, and generations later Heber the Kenite, of the children of Hobab, pitches his tent by the oak in Zaanannim when Deborah and Barak fight Sisera.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Hobab's story is about a man from outside Israel who is invited in, and God uses outsiders more often than we think. I hold that Moses asking for his help is no weakness, because God gives His people guides from unexpected places.
